title: How do we take away a bracket of two prices?
description: A shopper buys two items and pays one hundred rupees, and the change is found by taking away the prices one at a time. This shows that a minus sign before a bracket changes the signs inside. Keeko's doubt is that taking away the bracket means taking away the first price and adding the second.
teaching_notes: One idea: a minus sign before a bracket takes away everything inside it, so each term inside becomes a minus. Ask the child to find the change both ways and compare.

source: Find 100 − (15 + 56) by taking the two prices away one at a
video_script.why: The child sees a bracket after a minus sign opened by taking away the two prices one at a time, and checks it against working the bracket first.
video_script.substitution: Change the amount paid and the two prices and the method stays the same: take away each price in turn.
video_script.anchor: a shopper at a counter with a biscuit packet, a toor dal packet and a hundred rupee note
video_script.wrong_answer: taking away the bracket means taking away fifteen and adding fifty six
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes away the first price and then adds the second price back, so the change comes out more than the shopper paid.
video_script.payoff_line: The change is twenty nine rupees either way.

final_answer.spoken: one hundred minus the bracket fifteen plus fifty six is one hundred minus fifteen minus fifty six, which is twenty nine

names.{{NAME_2}}: everyday child, not a character of the book

video_script.design: One idea: a minus sign before a bracket changes the signs of the terms inside. The shop counter stays in the anchor band; the working band shows each step. Keeko's doubt: take away the first price and add the second.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; {{NAME_2}} at a shop counter with a biscuit packet marked ₹15 and a toor dal packet marked ₹56; a ₹100 note in hand

marks.m1: the small title card From your book appears
marks.m3: the biscuit packet ₹15 and the toor dal packet ₹56 appear
marks.m5: a question mark appears over the counter

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>{{NAME_2}} goes to a shop.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>A biscuit packet costs fifteen rupees, and a toor dal packet costs fifty six.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>{{NAME_2}} pays with a note of one hundred rupees.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>How can we find the change by taking away the two prices one at a time?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 100 − (15 + 56) with the bracket holding both prices; a minus sign before the bracket pointing at both prices

marks.m2: the bracket is ringed round both prices
marks.m3: the minus sign before the bracket points at both prices

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The shopper pays one hundred rupees and buys both items.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The bracket holds the cost of both items together.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The minus sign before it takes away both prices.

beats.on_screen: Given: paid ₹100; biscuit packet ₹15; toor dal packet ₹56

marks.m2: the two prices are written under it

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, the shopper pays one hundred rupees.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The prices are fifteen rupees and fifty six rupees.

beats.on_screen: To find: 100 − (15 + 56) by taking away one price at a time; compare with the bracket first

marks.m2: the words compare with the bracket first are added

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the change by taking away one price at a time.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Then we compare it with working the bracket first.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: take away the first price: 100 − 15 = 85

marks.m2: 85 is labelled the money still owed to the shopper

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, take away the biscuit packet.
One hundred minus fifteen is eighty five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>That is the change if only the biscuits were bought.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: take away the second price from what is left: 85 − 56
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, the toor dal is also bought, so take its price from what is left.
That is eighty five minus fifty six.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 100 − (15 + 56) = 100 − 15 − 56; the signs of 15 and 56 inside the bracket are both minus now

marks.m2: the plus before 15 and the plus before 56 inside the bracket turn into minus signs

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, we did one hundred minus fifteen minus fifty six.
That equals one hundred minus the bracket fifteen plus fifty six.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>When the minus sign sits before the bracket, the signs inside change.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check, bracket first: 15 + 56 = 71, then 100 − 71; compare with 85 − 56

marks.m2: 100 − 71 is written beside 85 − 56 and the two are compared

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check by working the bracket first.
Fifteen plus fifty six is seventy one.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Compare one hundred minus seventy one with eighty five minus fifty six.
Both give the same number.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>The change is twenty nine rupees either way.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One hundred minus the bracket fifteen plus fifty six equals one hundred minus fifteen minus fifty six.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the counter
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 100 − 15 + 56; the bubble is struck through; the shopper would get back ₹56 more; both prices are taken away

marks.m2: the bubble is struck through and the extra ₹56 is marked
marks.m3: both prices are shown taken away from the ₹100 note

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks taking away the bracket means taking away fifteen and adding fifty six.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But then {{NAME_2}} would get fifty six rupees back for buying the toor dal.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Both prices are taken away.
